subject: Request for fixed-sum exit option and penalty escrow
messages:
From: Emma Carter <emma@healthtechlabs.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@healthtechlabs.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: SLA remedies and exit options

Aisha —

Thanks for the demo last week. We're close on product fit, but procurement had a few non-negotiable ask items for the contract before we can move to signature:

1) A fixed-sum early exit option: HealthTech needs the unilateral right to terminate for repeated unavailability and receive a fixed payout (equal to 3 months of committed fees) rather than only service credits.
2) An escrowed fee-at-risk: upon signature HealthTech wants 25% of the first-year committed spend placed in escrow to be released back to us if SLA targets are met; otherwise funds are released per a clear penalty schedule.
3) Liquidated damages for catastrophic incidents (data corruption/loss) — capped but cash-based.

I attached a simple showback of our expected billings and a short rationale. We recognize these are stronger than Redwood's public terms (credits-first), but because this is a platform used against production clinical pipelines, our risk tolerance is low.

Can you confirm whether Redwood will consider cash remedies + escrow? If you can't make those concessions, we need termination rights tied to multiple SLO misses with a meaningful cash remedy.

Thanks,
Emma Carter
Director, Procurement
HealthTech Labs
Attachment: HealthTech_SLA_Showback.xlsx
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Emma Carter <emma@healthtechlabs.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T11:38:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA remedies and exit options

Emma —

Thanks for the clear summary and the showback — appreciated. Short answer: we understand the ask but can't move to a blanket fixed-sum exit or large unrestricted liquidated damages without a few guardrails. That said, we want to find a path to close this deal. A few high-level options we can put on the table immediately:

- Escrow alternative: Redwood can support a one-time escrow equal to up to 1 month of committed spend (instead of 25%) tied to a narrowly-defined set of SLOs for availability and latency on the production endpoint. Release rules can be automated against SLO checks.

- Cash remedy cap: we can agree to a cash remedy (not just credits) but limited to a pre-agreed capped amount and only for specified severity incidents (e.g., production-wide outages >30 minutes, or data-loss events).

- Termination: unilateral termination right can be considered, but only after a 3-strike pattern (e.g., 3 qualifying SLO failures within a 90-day rolling window) with cure windows and the ability for Redwood to restore service or provide backstop mitigation.

I looped in Neha (Legal) and Ben (Sales Ops) to sketch a concrete proposal and calculate the numeric caps based on your showback. If any of these adjustments look acceptable, I'll follow up with a redline and an illustrative penalty schedule.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-06T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA remedies and exit options — draft penalty schedule

Aisha / Ben —

Drafting notes for the proposed counterparty-friendly but protectively scoped cash remedies:

- Escrow: agree to an escrow equal to 1x monthly committed spend. Escrow to be replenished only if expended for qualifying remedies; otherwise returned at the 12-month anniversary.

- Qualifying incidents: define narrow bins — (P1 outage: total service unavailability impacting >50% of requests for >30 minutes), (P2 sustained latency degradation: p95 latency > 5x baseline for >60 minutes), (Data integrity incident: confirmed data loss/corruption). Only P1 and Data integrity permit cash remedies; P2 triggers credits.

- Cash remedies: for P1 incidents, allow fixed cash payout capped at 1 month of committed spend per incident, cumulative cap of 3 months over any 12-month period. For Data integrity, provide a separate capped liquidated damages bucket (subject to investigation and remediation verification).

- Cure and dispute: permit Redwood a 72-hour cure window for P1 before cash remedy is payable, plus an independent joint post-incident review to validate root cause. Termination right for HealthTech only after 3 qualifying P1 or Data Integrity incidents within a 90-day rolling window, and after exhaustion of cure opportunities.

- Auditability: automated SLO metrics to be shared via our Console, and DocuSign/Drive links recorded for payment/escrow triggers.

I've attached a short PDF with the numeric schedule for review. If Sales is comfortable with these limits we can put them in the SOW as Exhibit A and push to redline.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
Attachment: Proposed_Penalty_Schedule_v2.pdf
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Emma Carter <emma@healthtechlabs.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA remedies and exit options — Redwood counterproposal

Emma —

Thanks for your patience while we worked this through internally. Based on your showback and the risk profile you described, Redwood can accept a limited cash-based path alongside credits under these terms (summary below). If this is acceptable, we'll convert to a small exhibit for the SOW and circulate a clean redline.

Summary of Redwood counterproposal (short):
- Escrow: 1x monthly committed spend deposited at signature; returned at 12 months if unused.
- Cash remedies: P1 outage payout = 1 month committed spend per incident (payable after 72-hour cure and joint incident validation); cumulative cap = 3 months in any 12-month period.
- Data integrity: separate liquidated-damages bucket — cash payout subject to investigation and agreed cap (proposed: up to 2 months committed spend).
- Latency/Sustained degradation: service credits only (as a % of monthly bill), not cash.
- Termination: HealthTech may terminate after 3 qualifying P1 or Data Integrity incidents within a 90-day rolling window, after cure periods and remediation steps.

Next steps: if you confirm this structure I'll send Exhibit A (penalty schedule) and a short doc showing the escrow flow (Drive link included). We will also include standard dispute resolution language and a requirement for joint post-incident RCA before payout.

Would you like us to proceed to a DocuSign packet, or do you prefer another round of redlines from procurement?

Best regards,
Aisha
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0132
